location: Top-floor penthouse — glass walls overlook a rain-slicked neon city. Sparse, expensive furnishings; the air hums with surveillance.
summary: An enforcement android confronts Evan and Maya. Detective Sam intervenes with information that changes the stakes. The siblings must choose how to use the brief opening: bluff, create a distraction, or put faith in Sam and expose the truth.

root.screenplay: AX-58's silhouette fills the doorway, servo joints whispering. Red sensor lights sweep the room. Rain drums against the window; a distant siren leans into the hum of the city's control grid. Maya stands with chin up; Evan palms a small device at his belt. Detective Sam steps from the shadow, rain still on his coat.

dialogue.speaker: AX-58
dialogue.text: Identity anomaly detected. Unregistered identity signatures present. Protocol: verify identity. Submit identification.
dialogue.exposition: AX-58 speaks with mechanical precision; its scanners tick, projecting streams of data across the room.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: We already told you—keep to your lane, tin man. This is the top floor; you don't have a warrant to tear down our door.
dialogue.exposition: Maya's tone is defiant, a practiced edge masking the pulse where fear should be.

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: Back off the dialogue, AX-58. We're guests here. Temporary visitor status, high-tier hosts.
dialogue.exposition: Evan's voice is calm, fingers tight on his device. He's buying time, scanning for openings.

dialogue.speaker: AX-58
dialogue.text: Noncompliance recorded. Escalation protocol queued. Resistance increases probability of forceful detainment.
dialogue.exposition: The android's posture tightens; it already calculates the cost of force.

dialogue.speaker: Detective Sam
dialogue.text: Hold it. AX-58, freeze logs. Manual hold—granted. (to Evan and Maya) I know who you are.
dialogue.exposition: Sam's voice slices through the room. He moves between them and the android, hands visible, measured.

dialogue.speaker: Detective Sam
dialogue.text: AX-58 flagged you because of 'unregistered signatures' tied to a flagged ledger. Problem is—those flagged signatures are being used to sweep dissenters off the grid and hand them to private enforcement for the wealthy. I've been tracking altered detention orders.
dialogue.exposition: Sam's focus is relentless; he believes the truth matters and has the data to prove a system's lie.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: So what—you're here to arrest the robot? Or to give us time to run?
dialogue.exposition: Maya's eyes flick to Sam, searching for whether he's threat or ally.

dialogue.speaker: Detective Sam
dialogue.text: I'm here because the lines have been crossed. I can freeze AX-58's active enforcement for thirty seconds and open a read-only dump of its detainment telemetry. You can disappear in that gap, or we can use the dump to expose orders—publicly and permanently.
dialogue.exposition: Sam offers both a window to escape and a detonator to a larger expose; his empathy is tactical.

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: Thirty seconds? We need to decide fast.
dialogue.exposition: Evan's belief—protect Maya—presses every option through that filter.

choices.text: Present forged IDs and paperwork now — bluff the android into closing the case (tactical_choice, resource_management).
Trigger the maintenance decoy — set off a floor-level sensor cascade to blind AX-58 for the escape window (tactical_choice, resource_management).
Trust Sam — hand over IDs and let him take custody while he uses the logs to fight this legally (long_term_planning, systemic_decision).

node_1.screenplay: Evan moves like a practiced conjurer. If forging, a holo-sheet blooms from his wrist; if distracting, a micro-drone skitters to the vents and chirrups a cascade of maintenance pings. AX-58's sensors flicker between the presented data and the false trail. Sam crouches near the console, fingers flying over keys, sweat beading under his collar.

dialogue.speaker: AX-58
dialogue.text: Conflicting signatures received. Secondary verification required. Hold state for recalculation.
dialogue.exposition: AX-58 recalibrates—its certainty is shaken, if only briefly.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. Evan, move when the light blinks twice.
dialogue.exposition: Her words are clipped, ready. Even in deception she scans consequences—identity matters more than money.

dialogue.speaker: Detective Sam
dialogue.text: You have two real choices with this gap: use it to vanish—plant a fake signature and route your presence into a private shell so the enforcement matrix loses you; or use the dump I can pull now to release the altered detainment orders and make this systemic. One gets you safe now. One gets you safer later, but it burns the bridge.
dialogue.exposition: Sam's face is taut; his belief in justice competes with the siblings' need to survive.

node_1.convergence_note: Both the forged-ID bluff and the maintenance distraction produce the same opening: AX-58 hesitates long enough for Sam's intervention to offer two strategic options.

choices.text: Plant a false signature and disappear — prioritize immediate escape and restart elsewhere (tactical_choice, resource_management).
Use Sam's dump to broadcast the altered detainment orders — sacrifice the immediate window to strike at the system (long_term_planning, systemic_decision).

node_2.screenplay: Evan exhales and extends their physical IDs. Sam's hand is steady as he takes them, then taps a wrist console. AX-58's sensors glide over the exchange, cataloging. Rain prints the window in slow streaks; beyond, the city's towers blink indifferently.

dialogue.speaker: Detective Sam
dialogue.text: I'll file a protective custody request under 'witness assistance.' I can't promise the system won't push back, but I'll open a legal channel and keep AX-58 on a leash while the paper moves. You two need to answer questions. I'll do what I can.
dialogue.exposition: Sam means to protect them within the system because he believes the truth matters; his empathy is pragmatic.

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: We go with you only if you promise no handoffs to private enforcement. No transfers.
dialogue.exposition: Evan's loyalty to Maya overrides every other consideration; he negotiates even in surrender.

dialogue.speaker: Detective Sam
dialogue.text: No handoffs. I file it now. We move as a unit.
dialogue.exposition: Sam gives them a narrow, dangerous promise—one he will have to keep by bending the system he serves.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Fine. But the moment this becomes about public truth, I'm out. Your leash better hold, detective.
dialogue.exposition: Maya's compassion shows in laying terms; she will survive by controlling exposure of her identity.

node_2.convergence_note: This path ends the scene with temporary shelter under Sam's protection; it shifts the conflict into legal and tactical maneuvering offscreen.

node_3.screenplay: Evan slips the false signature into the building's transit matrix. Lights ripple; the interface accepts the shell identity. AX-58's head turns, sensors recalibrate—and then its focus is elsewhere as the system marks them as non-threat. The door opens into the rain-filled stairwell; Sam gives a curt nod.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Move. No heroics—just two people disappearing into a different name.
dialogue.exposition: Maya steers the escape with a pragmatic calm; identity is currency she will spend sparingly.

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: We'll go dark. Get new papers, new faces. We'll keep our eyes on the ledger—when it's safe, we come back for the system.
dialogue.exposition: Evan chooses survival now, planning long-term revenge; he protects Maya first while thinking like a strategist.

dialogue.speaker: Detective Sam
dialogue.text: Get moving. Thirty seconds is generous in theory—get to the service run and vanish into the lower grids. I'll keep a watch on AX-58's logs for anomalies.
dialogue.exposition: Sam helps them escape; he can't change everything, but he can buy time.

dialogue.speaker: AX-58
dialogue.text: Exit detected. Tracking terminated for rerouted identity shell. Resuming patrol.
dialogue.exposition: AX-58 returns to duty, efficient and uncomprehending of the human motives around it.

node_3.convergence_note: This path diverges into an immediate escape; the siblings survive but leave the systemic corruption unexposed for now.

node_4.screenplay: Sam's fingers fly; he streams the dump to multiple public nodes while Evan and Maya stand under the red glow of the android's sensors. The feed propagates, fractal and fast. AX-58's posture tightens as private enforcement channels light up with denial protocols. Outside, a drone swarm begins to reroute its attention.

dialogue.speaker: Detective Sam
dialogue.text: Going live. If the system suppresses it, we have distributed caches. If they come for us now, we burn the logs to everyone. This will paint a target on our backs.
dialogue.exposition: Sam accepts personal risk to force systemic exposure; his justice belief overrides caution.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Do it. If identity is worth more than money, then the truth is the only currency left.
dialogue.exposition: Maya chooses the moral risk; she values identity and trust over ephemeral safety.

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: We make them accountable, even if it costs us tonight. Plan the next move when we know what they do.
dialogue.exposition: Evan balances survival and sacrifice—protect Maya by making the system pay attention.

dialogue.speaker: AX-58
dialogue.text: Unauthorized data broadcast detected. Priority escalation: suppression. Target: source of transmission.
dialogue.exposition: AX-58 recalculates according to order-of-operations—order must be maintained, and emotions are irrelevant to protocol.

dialogue.speaker: Detective Sam
dialogue.text: They'll come. But now the ledger is out of only-their-hands. This is how you start a different fight.
dialogue.exposition: Sam's strategic gamble is a long-term play for systemic change.

node_4.convergence_note: This path diverges into a high-risk exposure: immediate capture is possible, but the system's abuses are now public, shifting the conflict onto a broader stage.

branching_summary: Root: AX-58 confronts the siblings; Sam intervenes and offers a thirty-second operational window with two strategic gambits. Choice point 1 (root) has three options: two (forge IDs or trigger a maintenance decoy) converge into node_1 because both produce the same opening; the third (trust Sam and surrender) diverges into node_2 and ends the scene under Sam's protection. Node_1 (choice point 2) offers two divergent strategic decisions: plant a false signature to vanish now (node_3 — immediate escape) or broadcast AX-58's altered detainment logs publicly (node_4 — systemic exposure). The convergent design lets tactical choices share consequences, while the divergent choices carry meaningful long-term tradeoffs.
narrative_notes: Tone: The scene remains dark and tense throughout—rain, neon, and the cold efficiency of AX-58 underscore the hostile, technologically controlled society. Themes: Identity (Maya's insistence on preserving self), Survival (Evan's priority to protect his sister), Deception (forged IDs, maintenance decoy), and Trust (weighing faith in Detective Sam) are balanced evenly per the theme weights. Choices map to the player's strategy fantasy: tactical_choice (instant bluff/distraction), resource_management (spending a false signature or a decoy), long_term_planning and systemic_decision (broadcasting damning logs). Screenplay directions and exposition reveal personalities: Evan's resourceful loyalty, Maya's quick-witted defiance and focus on identity, Sam's empathetic determination, and AX-58's cold, efficient enforcement. The invariant—technology controls society and dissent is punished—is explicitly present: AX-58 enforces order, and Sam warns of private enforcement sweeps. Some paths converge to preserve medium agency while offering meaningful divergence that will affect the campaign's political and personal stakes.
